title: First Win with AI
subtitle: 10 minutes to something that runs
description: The easiest Teachy on-ramp. Open an AI, ask for one tiny thing, and see it run — so you feel the loop before the full Use AI to Code path.
learningOutcomes: Open an AI that can help you write code
See a result run or preview on screen

goals.title: Open your AI
goals.goal: Have Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor open so you can ask it to build something tiny.
goals.coachAsk: They're starting First Win. Explain from zero if needed: an “AI chat” is a website or app where you type what you want and it writes back — Claude (claude.ai) and ChatGPT are popular ones; Cursor is an app that helps you write code with AI. Help them open whichever is easiest. Point at what to click. Don't assume they know any of these names.
goals.doneWhen: An AI chat or AI coding tool is open and recognizable on screen.
tips: Claude or ChatGPT in the browser is perfect
Cursor works too if they already have it

goals.title: Ask for one tiny thing
goals.goal: Send one clear prompt for a tiny project — tip calculator, to-do, or hello page.
goals.coachAsk: Explain what a “prompt” is if needed — it's just the message you type to the AI, like asking a friend. Help them send one clear tiny ask (suggest: make a single HTML tip calculator — HTML is a simple webpage file). Point at where they type and how to send. Prompt chips may be on the HUD.
goals.doneWhen: A clear tiny-project prompt is visible as typed or sent in the AI chat.

goals.title: See it run
goals.goal: Open or preview the result so something real is on screen.
goals.coachAsk: The AI should have answered with code or steps. Explain if needed: “running” means opening the result so they can see it work — often save as a .html file and open it in a browser (Chrome, Safari, etc.). Point at the next move to actually see it.
goals.doneWhen: A running or previewed result is visible — browser page, preview, or clear live output.
